narrativeReportMd:
# Coverage R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Coverage` has material local breaking changes in the R6 ballot build. The artifact identity is stable, but R6 adds a mandatory `kind`, removes/splits the required R4 `payor` model, and changes `subscriberId` and `class.value` from primitive strings to `Identifier`. These are direct validation and code-generation breaks for common R4 Coverage instances.

## Scope
The assessment used the R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, the batch manifest assignment, and directly relevant local ValueSets/CodeSystems. Inherited base-resource changes such as `language`, extension rules, modifierExtension summary behavior, and base `dom-*`/`ele-1` constraints are out of scope for this Coverage report.

## Main migration themes
The largest theme is a payer model redesign: R4 required `payor` as one-or-more references to Organization, Patient, or RelatedPerson; R6 replaces that with required `kind`, optional/constrained `insurer`, and `paymentBy` for self-pay parties. A second theme is richer identifier modeling: subscriber IDs and class values are no longer scalar strings. A third theme is R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can express payer kind, payer responsibility, multiple subscriber identifiers with systems/assigners, Identifier-valued class values, InsurancePlan references, status reasons, and cost-to-beneficiary dimensions that R4 cannot carry without extensions or loss.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `Coverage.kind` becoming mandatory, `Coverage.payor` being removed and split, `Coverage.subscriberId` changing from `string` to repeating `Identifier`, and `Coverage.class.value` changing from `string` to `Identifier`. Each affects JSON shape, generated models, validation, FHIRPath expressions, and migration transforms.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for payer migration. An R4 `payor` reference to an Organization can often become R6 `insurer` with `kind = insurance`, while Patient or RelatedPerson payors usually imply self-pay `paymentBy`. Multiple R4 payors, non-insurance agreements, and R6 `kind = other` need policy decisions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some goals appear clinically or operationally justified, especially using `Identifier` for values that need systems and assigners. However, several changes could have been less disruptive through additive elements, choice types, or deprecation periods.

## Follow-up analysis
A cross-version ConceptMap or implementation guide mapping for Coverage payer/kind and Identifier conversions would materially improve migration reliability. Terminology expansion comparison for Coverage-related ValueSets would improve confidence in binding-level conclusions.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Coverage has high-impact local R4-to-R6 breaks: mandatory `kind`, removal/split of required `payor`, and string-to-`Identifier` shape changes for `subscriberId` and `class.value`. The largest uncertainty is not whether these changes exist, but how official guidance expects ambiguous payer scenarios to migrate.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should first classify each Coverage as insurance, self-pay, or other; then map R4 `payor` to R6 `insurer` or `paymentBy`; then convert scalar string identifiers into `Identifier` objects. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for payer kind/responsibility, multiple or qualified identifiers, class identifier metadata, optional `statusReason`, `insurancePlan`, and expanded cost-to-beneficiary dimensions.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both assigned StructureDefinitions and package indexes were available locally and agree on identity. Confidence is medium for terminology and intent: most existing Coverage ValueSet compose definitions are unchanged, but expansions were not run and no official narrative diff or ConceptMap was supplied.

findings.title: Coverage.kind is a new mandatory required-code element with cross-element constraints

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Coverage did not require an explicit discriminator for insurance, self-pay, or other payment kind.

newState.summary: R6 adds `Coverage.kind` as 1..1 `code` with a required binding to coverage-kind and local error constraints.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R6 CodeSystem defines `insurance`, `self-pay`, and `other`; no R4 equivalent element existed and no terminology expansion was run.

constraints.human: When patient is insured, insurer must exist.
When patient is self-pay, paymentBy must exist.

semanticText.definition: The nature of the coverage be it insurance, or cash payment such as self-pay.
semanticText.requirements: This is used to implement conformance on other elements.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes every Coverage declare whether it is insurance, self-pay, or another payment arrangement. The value drives local constraints on `insurer` and `paymentBy`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break because every R4 Coverage instance lacks `kind`, while R6 requires `kind` with a required code. It also affects runtime models and enum handling. In the reverse direction, R4 has no native place for the explicit R6 kind, so a lossless R6-to-R4 transform needs an extension or profile convention.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying insurance versus self-pay can change billing workflow, claim routing, patient liability handling, and payer coordination.

justification.inferredGoal: Disambiguate insurance, self-pay, and other payment arrangements and use that discriminator to validate payer elements.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `kind` optional or profile-required first, but that would not fully achieve base R6 discriminator validation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of explicitly distinguishing insurance, self-pay, and other payment arrangements is reasonable because the value drives payer conformance and billing behavior. The breakage is material because every R4 Coverage lacks `kind`, but an optional-only transition would not meet the core R6 goal of having base instances carry the discriminator needed for uniform `insurer` and `paymentBy` validation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would add `kind` as optional, perhaps with best-practice warnings or profile-level requirements during a transition. That preserves R4 instances, but only partially meets the goal: base R6 Coverage could still omit the discriminator, leaving applications unable to reliably apply the insurance versus self-pay constraints.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Less breakage would leave legacy Coverage instances unclassified and weaken insurer/paymentBy base constraints.

evidence.detail: No R4 element with id `Coverage.kind` exists.
R6 adds `Coverage.kind` with min 1, max 1, type code, required binding to `coverage-kind`, and local constraints `cov-insured-1` and `cov-self-pay-1`.
The R6 local CodeSystem contains `insurance`, `self-pay`, and `other`.

examples.examplesMd: The example is illustrative and focuses on the changed fields. A complete migration must also remove R4 `payor` and satisfy the R6 payer constraints.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a mandatory `Coverage.kind` discriminator. This means an R4 Coverage that otherwise contains the required R4 fields cannot validate as R6 until a migration determines whether it represents insurance, self-pay, or another payment arrangement. The value is not only descriptive: the R6 StructureDefinition attaches error constraints that require `insurer` for insurance and `paymentBy` for self-pay.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances become R6-invalid because the required `kind` element is absent. Strict parsers and generated R6 classes must now carry a non-null enum/code. R6 instances can be downgraded to R4 only by dropping `kind` or preserving it in an extension, so the transform is not semantically lossless.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each Coverage before conversion. Organization payors will often map to `kind = insurance` plus `insurer`; Patient or RelatedPerson payors will often map to `kind = self-pay` plus `paymentBy.party`. Do not blindly default every record to `insurance`; test self-pay, patient-pay agreements, absent/ambiguous payor data, and `other` payer scenarios.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic goal appears sound, but making the discriminator mandatory in the base resource is disruptive. A backward-compatible alternative would have made it optional or profile-required first, preserving R4 data while encouraging migration. The tradeoff is that base R6 validation could not enforce the insurer/paymentBy split uniformly.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed where R4 `payor` does not clearly identify an Organization insurer or a self-pay party.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds a new mandatory `Coverage.kind` discriminator with a required coverage-kind binding and error constraints that use it to separate insurance from self-pay. An R4 Coverage has no such element, so a direct structural migration must classify the coverage before it can validate. That is a real break for billing data, but the R6 goal is coherent: without a base discriminator, generic validators cannot consistently enforce the new `insurer` versus `paymentBy` model.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has no `Coverage.kind` element.
R6 `Coverage.kind` is 1..1 `code` with required binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/coverage-kind|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R6 local constraints `cov-insured-1` and `cov-self-pay-1` require `insurer` for insurance and `paymentBy` for self-pay.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Coverage is supplied as R4 FMM 2 and trial-use. That is neutral stability pressure: it does not erase a central billing migration burden, but it also does not create a normative presumption against the change.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Coverage that otherwise maps forward lacks the required `kind` code, and generated R6 models also need a non-null discriminator value.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could have made `kind` optional, warning-level, or profile-required during a transition. That would preserve old instances but would not meet the same base-R6 goal of making every Coverage computably classifiable for the insurer/paymentBy constraints.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly treats this as high-impact with only a partial less-breaking alternative, but the fresh path-level judgment is that the mandatory discriminator is proportionate rather than a design issue to revisit.

findings.title: Required R4 Coverage.payor was removed and split into insurer/paymentBy semantics

oldState.summary: R4 required `Coverage.payor` as 1..* Reference(Organization | Patient | RelatedPerson).

semanticText.definition: The program or plan underwriter or payor including both insurance and non-insurance agreements, such as patient-pay agreements.
semanticText.comment:
May provide multiple identifiers such as insurance company identifier or business identifier (BIN number).
For selfpay it may provide multiple paying persons and/or organizations.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used one required repeating element for insurers, underwriters, and non-insurance payors. It could point to organizations, patients, or related persons.

newState.summary: R6 has no `Coverage.payor`; it adds `Coverage.insurer` 0..1 Reference(Organization) and `Coverage.paymentBy` 0..* with mandatory `paymentBy.party` Reference(Patient | RelatedPerson | Organization). `Coverage.kind` constraints govern which element is allowed or required.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates the issuer of an insurance policy from parties making self-pay payments. It also narrows the insurance issuer to an Organization reference and allows self-pay responsibility text.

facts.newValue: 0..* BackboneElement with party 1..1 Reference(Patient|RelatedPerson|Organization) and optional responsibility

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `insurer` definition reuses the issuer/payor language for insurance organizations, while `paymentBy` carries the R4 self-pay/non-insurance paying-party semantics. The split is strongly indicated by definitions, target profiles, and the new `kind` constraints.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard R4-to-R6 break because R4 instances must contain `payor`, but R6 no longer defines that element. A strict R6 validator will reject the unknown property and also require the new payer model to satisfy `kind` constraints. It is also a high round-trip risk: R6 `paymentBy.responsibility`, `kind`, and the insurer/self-pay distinction have no native R4 slots.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The payer element is central to claim routing, coordination of benefits, and patient-pay workflows; an incorrect split can change who is billed or where claims are sent.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate insurance issuer data from self-pay/non-insurance payment responsibility and make payer semantics more explicit.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `payor` while adding `kind`, `insurer`, and `paymentBy`, but this would duplicate payer representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 `payor` element combined insurer, self-pay, and non-insurance payment concepts in one required field. Splitting those concepts is a reasonable base-model goal, and the old shape could not express `paymentBy.responsibility` or cleanly distinguish an insurance issuer from a self-pay party. Keeping the old element would have reduced immediate migration failures, but the tradeoff is substantial for a central billing field.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 design could have kept `Coverage.payor` as deprecated and added the more precise payer fields, with invariants or guidance discouraging mixed use. That alternative is only partial because it creates same-resource duplicate representations of the payer. Conflicting `payor`, `insurer`, and `paymentBy` values would create validation ambiguity, claim-routing risk, and a real chance that deprecated payer representations never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Transition compatibility would reduce validation failures but preserve ambiguity and risk conflicting payer data indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 `Coverage.payor` exists with min 1, max *, and target profiles Organization, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
No R6 element with id `Coverage.payor` exists.
R6 adds `Coverage.insurer` 0..1 Reference(Organization) with issuer/payor definition text.
evidence.quote: The program or plan underwriter, payor, insurance company.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `paymentBy.party` 1..1 Reference(Patient | RelatedPerson | Organization) for non-insurance/self-pay parties.

paymentBy.responsibility: Patient pays the deductible and non-covered services.

examples.examplesMd: The mapping examples show common cases only. Multiple R4 payors, mixed Organization and person payors, and R6 `kind = other` need local policy decisions or extensions.

findings.narrativeMd: R4's required `payor` element was removed from Coverage and its semantics were split across R6 `insurer`, `paymentBy`, and the required `kind` discriminator. This is more than a rename: R4 allowed one or more Organization, Patient, or RelatedPerson references in a single required field; R6 permits only one Organization insurer for insurance and uses a separate repeating backbone for self-pay parties and responsibility text.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 Coverage containing the required `payor` property is not valid against the R6 StructureDefinition because `payor` is no longer defined. R6 validation also enforces combinations of `kind`, `insurer`, and `paymentBy`. Generated client code, serializers, search expressions, and FHIRPath rules that refer to `Coverage.payor` will break. R6-to-R4 conversion can map some parties back to `payor`, but loses `kind`, `paymentBy.responsibility`, and sometimes the distinction between insurance issuer and self-pay party.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build an explicit payer classifier. Map a single Organization payor to `kind = insurance` and `insurer` when it represents an insurance issuer. Map patient-pay or related-person payors to `kind = self-pay` and `paymentBy.party`. Preserve ambiguous or mixed cases with extensions, manual review queues, or implementation-guide-specific rules. Update searches, indexes, and business logic that used `Coverage.payor`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change likely addresses genuine ambiguity, but removing a required R4 element rather than deprecating it creates a hard break. An additive transition would have been possible by keeping `payor` while introducing the more precise fields, but it would have complicated validation and allowed conflicting representations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding should be reviewed with billing/domain experts, especially for non-insurance agreements, multiple payors, and `kind = other`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 required `Coverage.payor` as the payer/issuer reference, while R6 removes that path and splits the model into `insurer` for insurance and `paymentBy.party` for self-pay or non-insurance payment parties. This breaks wire format, FHIRPath, and generated APIs that refer to `payor`, and some mappings need business judgment. The old element was overloaded, though, and the R6 split addresses a real modeling problem around insurer versus patient or other self-pay responsibility.
keyEvidence: R4 `Coverage.payor` is 1..* Reference(Organization | Patient | RelatedPerson).
R6 has no `Coverage.payor` element.
R6 adds `Coverage.insurer` 0..1 Reference(Organization) and `Coverage.paymentBy.party` 1..1 Reference(Patient | RelatedPerson | Organization).
freshReview.fmmEffect: Coverage is FMM 2 and trial-use, so the maturity context is neutral. The central billing role raises practical migration importance, but FMM 2 does not by itself make the split unacceptable.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 JSON containing the required `payor` path is not an R6 Coverage, and client code, searches, mappings, and FHIRPath expressions using `Coverage.payor` must be rewritten.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `payor` as a deprecated alias or kept the old path while adding clarifying fields. That would preserve more R4 payloads, but it would duplicate the central payer representation, require conflict rules with `insurer` and `paymentBy`, and weaken the cleanup of an overloaded element.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high impact and partial alternative assessment match the independent review; the final judgment is that the break is real but likely justified by the model split.

findings.title: Coverage.subscriberId changed from a single string to repeating Identifier

semanticText.definition: The insurer assigned ID for the Subscriber.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented the subscriber ID as a single primitive string at JSON property `subscriberId`.

semanticText.definition: The insurer assigned ID for the Subscriber.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 represents subscriber IDs as one or more Identifier objects, enabling systems, types, periods, assigners, and multiple IDs.

facts.oldValue: subscriberId: string plus optional _subscriberId primitive extension

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON representation changes from a primitive scalar to a repeating complex datatype. An R4 instance with `subscriberId: "ABC"` is not valid R6, and R6 instances with multiple identifiers or Identifier metadata cannot be represented in R4 without loss.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Subscriber identifiers are commonly used for eligibility checks, claims, matching, and member lookup. Dropping system or assigning authority can create collisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow subscriber identifiers to carry system, type, assigner, period, and multiple values rather than a bare string.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 string `subscriberId` and add a new repeating Identifier-valued element for richer subscriber identifiers.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The move from a bare string to `Identifier` is semantically reasonable, but replacing a same-path primitive with a repeating complex datatype creates avoidable wire-format and generated-code breakage for a common field. The R6 goal of carrying systems, assigners, periods, and multiple subscriber identifiers could have been met by adding a new Identifier-valued element while retaining the R4 string for compatibility.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could retain `subscriberId` as a deprecated string and add an optional repeating `subscriberIdentifier` or similarly named Identifier element. New systems could use the richer element, while R4-valid instances would remain valid. The main tradeoff is duplicate representations and the need to define how to reconcile both fields, but that is a moderate long-term cost compared with invalidating existing scalar `subscriberId` data.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Additive modeling preserves old instances but needs duplicate-field and precedence rules while the string field is deprecated.

evidence.detail: R4 `Coverage.subscriberId` has max 1 and type string.
R6 `Coverage.subscriberId` has max * and type Identifier.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example also includes required R4 Coverage fields. The subscriberId-specific transform wraps the old string in an Identifier with `value`; systems and assigners require external knowledge.

findings.narrativeMd: `Coverage.subscriberId` keeps the same path but changes wire shape. R4 clients expect a scalar primitive string. R6 clients expect an array of `Identifier` objects. Because the path name is unchanged, this is especially hazardous for generated models and hand-written serializers that assume same-name fields are compatible across versions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid JSON with `subscriberId` as a string becomes R6-invalid due to type mismatch. R6 JSON with `subscriberId` as an array of Identifier objects is not R4-valid. Reverse conversion can choose one Identifier.value, but loses system, type, period, assigner, extensions, and additional repetitions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, wrap the old string as `subscriberId[0].value` and populate `system`, `type`, or `assigner` only when a reliable source exists. For R6-to-R4, define a deterministic selection rule and preserve unrepresented Identifier metadata with extensions or an audit trail. Update codegen, database columns, indexes, and search extraction logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer Identifier model is likely justified, but replacing a same-name primitive with a repeating complex datatype was avoidable. An additive field or transition profile would have reduced breakage at the cost of temporary duplication.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Coverage.subscriberId` changes from a single primitive string to a repeating `Identifier`. Any R4 instance with `subscriberId: "..."` needs a shape-changing transform before R6 validation, and reverse conversion from multiple or system-qualified identifiers can lose information. Supporting richer identifiers is a good goal for eligibility and claims workflows, but replacing the existing scalar path looks avoidable.
keyEvidence: R4 `Coverage.subscriberId` is 0..1 `string`.
R6 `Coverage.subscriberId` is 0..* `Identifier`.
The element requirements in both versions identify subscriber IDs as needed by insurers for correspondence and claims.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use makes this a neutral maturity case, but subscriber identifiers are central enough to Coverage exchange that a hard representation break still deserves scrutiny.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the JSON type changes from a primitive scalar to repeating complex Identifier objects; R6-to-R4 loss is also possible for systems, assigners, periods, extensions, and extra repetitions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible less-breaking base design would retain the R4 string path and add a new optional repeating Identifier element, or otherwise stage the richer representation. The tradeoff is duplicate identifier representations and precedence rules, but that cost seems modest compared with breaking a common member-lookup field.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high-impact and Yes less-breaking-alternative assessment is supported by the fresh review.

findings.title: Coverage.class.value changed from string to Identifier

semanticText.definition: The alphanumeric string value associated with the insurer issued label.
semanticText.comment: For example, the Group or Plan number.

oldState.narrativeMd: Each R4 class component carried its required class value as a primitive string.

semanticText.definition: The alphanumeric identifier associated with the insurer issued label.
semanticText.comment: For example, the Group or Plan number.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires each class component to carry an Identifier object instead of a bare string.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element is still required when `Coverage.class` is present, but the JSON type changed from scalar string to complex Identifier. Existing R4 class entries therefore fail R6 validation until transformed. Reverse conversion can preserve Identifier.value but loses additional Identifier metadata.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Class values such as group, plan, or BIN identifiers affect benefit determination and routing; losing the assigning system can cause ambiguity.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent coverage class values as identifiers with assigning systems and richer metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Coverage.class.value` as the R4 string and add a separate Identifier-valued class element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing class values as identifiers is a reasonable improvement, especially for group, plan, or routing values that need an assigning system. However, directly changing the same required element from string to `Identifier` breaks existing Coverage.class entries even though the richer metadata could have been added without replacing the R4 wire shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could keep `Coverage.class.value` as a deprecated string and add `Coverage.class.identifier` or another optional Identifier-valued child for systems that know the assigning namespace. This would preserve most R4-valid instances while meeting the goal for new data. The tradeoff is duplicate same-resource representations; implementations would need precedence rules, and deprecated string values could persist for a long time.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The alternative preserves class entries but creates duplicate class value representations and reconciliation rules.

evidence.detail: R4 `Coverage.class.value` is 1..1 string.
evidence.quote: The alphanumeric string value associated with the insurer issued label.

evidence.detail: R6 `Coverage.class.value` is 1..1 Identifier.
evidence.quote: The alphanumeric identifier associated with the insurer issued label.

examples.examplesMd: The transform wraps the R4 string as `class.value.value`; assigning system or assigner cannot be inferred from the R4 string alone.

findings.narrativeMd: Coverage class entries still have a required `value`, but R6 changes that value from a primitive string to an `Identifier`. This breaks same-path assumptions and affects systems that parse group, plan, class, sequence, or pharmacy routing values from Coverage.class.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 Coverage.class entry with `value: "GRP123"` becomes R6-invalid because R6 expects an Identifier object. An R6 Identifier-valued class can be downgraded to R4 only by choosing `Identifier.value` and losing system, type, period, assigner, and extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap each R4 class value string in an Identifier object. Where payer-specific namespaces are known, populate `Identifier.system` or `assigner`; otherwise leave only `value` and document the limitation. Update serializers, FHIRPath expressions, and database schema for nested Identifier fields.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This change is semantically reasonable but mechanically breaking. The same goal could have been achieved by an additive Identifier element or a transition period, at the cost of temporary duplication.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Coverage.class.value` remains required when a class component is present, but its type changes from string to `Identifier`. Existing R4 class components such as group or plan numbers therefore fail R6 validation unless transformed into Identifier objects. The forward transform is usually mechanical, but the base wire-format break appears larger than necessary for adding identifier metadata.
keyEvidence: R4 `Coverage.class.value` is 1..1 `string` with definition `The alphanumeric string value associated with the insurer issued label.`
R6 `Coverage.class.value` is 1..1 `Identifier` with definition `The alphanumeric identifier associated with the insurer issued label.`
Both versions describe the value as necessary to identify the policy, group, or plan.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Coverage is FMM 2/trial-use, so maturity does not strongly raise or lower the concern. The decision rests mainly on the direct type break and availability of a less-breaking design.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: R4 class entries with scalar `value` are not R6-shaped, and generated clients change from a string property to an Identifier object.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `class.value` as the legacy string and added an optional sibling for assigning system or full Identifier metadata. That would introduce possible duplication and matching rules, but it would preserve the required R4 field while enabling richer identifiers.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's high impact and Yes less-breaking alternative are consistent with this path-level assessment.

findings.title: Cost-to-beneficiary entries no longer require value[x] and gained additional benefit dimensions

oldState.summary: R4 `Coverage.costToBeneficiary.value[x]` was required 1..1 when a costToBeneficiary component was present; allowed types were Quantity(SimpleQuantity) or Money.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 cost-to-beneficiary components had to carry an amount or percentage.

newState.summary: R6 lowers `value[x]` to 0..1 with the same choice types, and adds optional `category`, `network`, `unit`, and `term` CodeableConcept elements under costToBeneficiary.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can describe benefit category/network/unit/term details even when an amount is not supplied.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Lowering the minimum is not an R4-to-R6 validation break; old populated values remain valid. The risk is reverse conversion and runtime assumptions: R6 cost components may omit `value[x]`, and new child dimensions have no R4 fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Patient cost-sharing and benefit terms affect financial responsibility estimates; dropping network/unit/term or accepting value-less entries can change interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow Coverage to express richer benefit cost context and cases where category/network/unit/term are known before the amount is known.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because this is a forward-compatible cardinality loosening plus optional R6 content, not an R4-to-R6 validation break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Lowering `value[x]` from 1..1 to 0..1 preserves R4 cost-to-beneficiary entries and lets R6 represent benefit category, network, unit, and term details before an amount is known. The resulting incompatibility is primarily reverse conversion: an R6 value-less cost component cannot be represented in base R4 without extensions or loss.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because existing R4 instances remain valid for this aspect. Keeping `value[x]` mandatory would improve downgrade symmetry but would block the R6 expressiveness goal rather than preserve additional R4 data.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is R6-to-R4 downgrade loss for value-less benefit dimensions, not breakage of R4 instances moving forward.

evidence.detail: R4 `value[x]` min is 1 and types are Quantity(SimpleQuantity) or Money.
R6 `value[x]` min is 0 with the same two choice types.
R6 adds optional costToBeneficiary category, network, unit, and term elements.

examples.examplesMd: This R6 fragment has a costToBeneficiary component with no amount. R4 requires `value[x]` for each component and has no native category/network/unit/term children.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens `costToBeneficiary`. Existing R4 entries with an amount or percentage still fit the R6 choice types, but R6 entries can now be valid with only contextual benefit dimensions and no value. That is important for reverse transforms and for application code that assumed a cost component always had an amount.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4-valid instance becomes invalid solely because of this cardinality decrease. Conversely, an R6-valid costToBeneficiary entry without `value[x]` is invalid in R4. New R6 dimensions are also not R4-representable except by extension or data loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, copy existing `value[x]`, `type`, and exception data unchanged. For R6-to-R4, either require `value[x]`, drop value-less entries, synthesize a value only with clear business rules, or preserve the entry and new dimensions in extensions. Add tests for cost entries with and without amounts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This is mostly an intentional widening rather than an R4-to-R6 break. The compatibility tradeoff is acceptable if R6 needs to represent benefit dimensions without known amounts, but it requires explicit downgrade policy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 lowers `Coverage.costToBeneficiary.value[x]` from required to optional and adds optional benefit dimensions under the same component. That is a widening change for R4-to-R6 migration: an R4 component that has the required value remains structurally acceptable on this path. New R6 value-less or more dimensioned components may not round-trip to R4 cleanly, but that is a reverse-conversion limitation rather than a base compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 `Coverage.costToBeneficiary.value[x]` is 1..1 Quantity(SimpleQuantity) or Money.
R6 `Coverage.costToBeneficiary.value[x]` is 0..1 with the same Quantity(SimpleQuantity) or Money choice types.
R6 adds optional `category`, `network`, `unit`, and `term` elements under `costToBeneficiary`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral here. Because the change is widening/additive for R4-to-R6, maturity does not create a reason to revisit it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can express cost components without `value[x]` or with additional dimensions that R4 cannot natively carry, but no R4-valid value on this path becomes R6-invalid.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed. Keeping `value[x]` mandatory would be more restrictive, not less breaking, and the added dimensions are optional.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly says there is no hard R4-to-R6 break, but I would downgrade the finding from a medium compatibility concern to no problem for this review.

findings.title: Coverage.status semantics now explicitly separate resource status from policy in-force period

oldState.summary: R4 `Coverage.status` was 1..1 required code bound to fm-status|4.0.1 with definition `The status of the resource instance.`

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

semanticText.definition: The status of the resource instance.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 already modeled Coverage.status as a resource-instance status and modifier, but the definition did not explicitly warn against using it as in-force coverage status.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same cardinality, type, required fm-status codes, modifier flag, and summary flag, but definition text states that status does not indicate whether the policy is in force; `period` conveys that. R6 also adds optional `statusReason`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local fm-status CodeSystem in both packages contains the same four codes: active, cancelled, draft, and entered-in-error. Expansion was not run.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

semanticText.definition: The status of the resource instance. The status element does not indicate whether the policy reflected in the instance is in-force at any particular point in time, that would be conveyed via the 'period' element.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 explicitly directs implementers not to infer policy in-force coverage from `status`; use `period` for that question. Optional `statusReason` can carry the reason for a status change.

facts.oldValue: The status of the resource instance.
facts.newValue: The status of the resource instance. The status element does not indicate whether the policy reflected in the instance is in-force at any particular point in time, that would be conveyed via the 'period' element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The computable status cardinality, type, required binding strength, modifier flag, summary flag, and local fm-status codes are materially unchanged. The risk is behavioral: systems that used `status = active` as proof that coverage is in force should instead evaluate `period` and local business rules. R6 `statusReason` has no native R4 field.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly treating an active resource as currently in-force could affect eligibility and billing decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify long-standing distinction between resource lifecycle status and coverage effective period, and add optional status change reason.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because the change is a semantic clarification and optional `statusReason` addition, not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design change.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 text clarifies that `Coverage.status` is resource lifecycle status rather than proof that the policy is currently in force, while preserving the required code shape and apparent code set. This clarification is safety-positive and does not invalidate R4 instances. Optional `statusReason` adds R6 expressiveness without forcing old data to change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the primary change is clarifying text plus optional content, a less-breaking base design is not applicable. Downgrade systems may carry `statusReason` in an extension, but that is an R6-to-R4 mitigation rather than a backward-compatible alternative to a breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The only material tradeoff is possible R6-to-R4 loss of optional `statusReason`; R4 status instances remain valid.

evidence.detail: R4 status definition is limited to resource-instance status.
evidence.quote: The status of the resource instance.

evidence.detail: R6 status definition adds that status does not indicate whether the policy is in force and points to `period`.
evidence.quote: does not indicate whether the policy reflected in the instance is in-force

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional `Coverage.statusReason` 0..1 string.
The available R4 and R6 local fm-status CodeSystems contain the same codes: active, cancelled, draft, entered-in-error.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no native `statusReason`; preserving it requires an extension or external audit/event record.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 clarifies that `Coverage.status` is not an in-force indicator for the policy. This may not change validation, but it can change business behavior for applications that equated `active` with currently usable coverage. The new optional `statusReason` also provides R6-only status context.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances do not fail R6 validation because of the status text change, and the required fm-status code set appears unchanged in the local CodeSystems. The compatibility risk is runtime semantic behavior and R6-to-R4 loss of `statusReason`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review eligibility, billing, and UI logic that uses `Coverage.status`. Treat `period` and payer-specific rules as the source for in-force determinations. Preserve `statusReason` during downgrade with an extension if the reason must survive R6-to-R4 exchange.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clarification is backward-compatible and safety-positive. It does not appear to require an alternative design beyond documenting the semantic distinction and optional status reason mapping.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confidence that this is a semantic clarification rather than a new normative rule would improve with narrative ballot change notes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The computable shape of `Coverage.status` is unchanged: it is still a required code with the same apparent fm-status choices. R6 adds prose clarifying that the status is the resource instance status and not proof that a policy is in force at a particular time. That may correct local business assumptions, but it does not make R4 instances invalid or create a new base validator requirement.
keyEvidence: R4 `Coverage.status` is 1..1 `code` with required `fm-status|4.0.1` binding and definition `The status of the resource instance.`
R6 `Coverage.status` remains 1..1 `code` with required `fm-status|6.0.0-ballot4` binding and adds text directing in-force evaluation to `period`.
The current report notes the local R4 and R6 fm-status CodeSystems contain the same codes: active, cancelled, draft, entered-in-error.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 2/trial-use is neutral. Since the change is a clarification rather than a structural or terminology restriction, stability pressure does not alter the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: implementations that treated `active` as in-force may need business-rule changes, but the base element cardinality, type, modifier status, and required code family are not materially narrowed.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No meaningful less-breaking base design is needed. Softer prose would be possible, but the R6 wording is already a clarification of resource-status semantics rather than a new computable constraint.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree there is no hard instance break, but I do not agree that this rises to a medium compatibility concern under the fresh-review rubric.

findings.title: R6 adds optional Coverage fields that are not natively representable in R4

oldState.summary: R4 had no native elements for status reason, InsurancePlan linkage, cost category/network/unit/term dimensions, or self-pay responsibility text.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 can only carry these concepts through extensions, adjacent resources, or local conventions.

newState.summary: R6 adds several optional local elements for status reason, InsurancePlan, cost dimensions, and payment responsibility.
newState.narrativeMd: These additions do not invalidate R4 data moving forward, but they create predictable loss when converting richer R6 data back to R4.

facts.newValue: extension/profile-specific mapping required for lossless downgrade

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions are not R4-to-R6 breaking by themselves. They matter for bidirectional systems: valid R6 Coverage instances can carry business data that an R4 Coverage cannot express without extensions or side-channel records.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of status reasons, plan linkage, cost benefit dimensions, or payment responsibility can affect billing explanations and patient financial responsibility.

justification.inferredGoal: Increase Coverage expressiveness for status lifecycle, insurance plan linkage, patient cost context, and self-pay responsibility.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because these are optional R6 additions and pure R6-to-R4 representability concerns.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional fields for status reason, insurance plan linkage, benefit dimensions, and payment responsibility does not break R4 instances migrating to R6. The goal of representing common Coverage details in the core R6 model is reasonable, and the incompatibility described by this finding is the expected lossiness of converting richer R6 content back to R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using only extensions for these concepts would make R6-to-R4 round-tripping more uniform, but it is not a backward-compatible alternative to an R4-to-R6 break because there is no such break here. Extension/backport strategies remain downgrade mitigations, while optional core elements are already forward-compatible for R4 data.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Core optional elements improve R6 consistency and discoverability but require extensions or loss when downgrading to R4.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional `Coverage.statusReason` 0..1 string.
R6 adds optional `Coverage.insurancePlan` 0..1 Reference(InsurancePlan).
R6 adds optional responsibility text under `paymentBy`.
No matching R4 elements exist for these optional R6 paths.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can keep the core Coverage only by dropping these fields or preserving them as extensions/profile-specific data.

findings.narrativeMd: Several R6 additions are not breaking when moving old R4 data forward, but they are important for systems that round-trip, downgrade, or maintain one canonical model for both versions. A valid R6 Coverage may contain details that R4 has no native element for.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators reject these R6-native paths unless they are transformed into extensions. The risk is not old-valid/new-invalid; it is R6-valid/not-R4-representable without loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define downgrade extensions or sidecar mappings for R6-only fields before enabling bidirectional exchange. For integrations that only consume R6, update generated models and serializers to include the new optional elements. For R4 partners, document which fields are dropped or extension-carried.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are the usual backward-compatible way to evolve a resource. The residual issue is inherent to cross-version downgrade, not a flaw in R6 forward compatibility.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The cited R6 fields are optional additions with no native R4 equivalents. They can matter to bidirectional converters because R6 data such as status reason, InsurancePlan linkage, or payment responsibility may need extensions or may be dropped when producing R4. They do not, however, make any R4 Coverage invalid in R6, and optional additive expressivity is normally the compatibility-preserving way to evolve a resource.
keyEvidence: R6 adds optional `Coverage.statusReason` 0..1 `string`.
R6 adds optional `Coverage.insurancePlan` 0..1 Reference(InsurancePlan).
R6 adds optional `Coverage.paymentBy.responsibility` 0..1 `string`; R4 has no matching native paths.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Coverage is FMM 2/trial-use, which is neutral. Because these are optional additions, FMM does not raise them into a design concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using the new optional fields cannot be represented in plain R4 without extensions or loss, but this is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not adding the fields would avoid reverse-mapping loss but would also forgo R6 expressivity. Making them optional is already the less-breaking base approach.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies reverse-conversion loss and no hard break, but the fresh judgment is no problem rather than a medium-impact concern.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag are stable. R6 package index confirms `StructureDefinition-Coverage.json` at the same canonical URL.
Aside from the handled payer remodel, target profiles for `policyHolder`, `subscriber`, `beneficiary`, and `contract` remain materially unchanged.

Existing Coverage bindings for `type`, `relationship`, `class.type`, `costToBeneficiary.type`, and `costToBeneficiary.exception.type` keep the same strength and ValueSet URL. `status` remains required and the local fm-status CodeSystem codes appear unchanged. Full terminology expansions were not run.

No material type-domain changes were found beyond `subscriberId` and `class.value`, which are reported as findings. The `costToBeneficiary.value[x]` choice types remain Quantity(SimpleQuantity) and Money.
No material local cardinality changes were found beyond mandatory `kind`, removed/split `payor`, repeating `subscriberId`, and lowered `costToBeneficiary.value[x]`, which are reported as findings.

The material local new constraints are `cov-insured-1` and `cov-self-pay-1` on `Coverage.kind`, reported above. Other observed `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraint expression/text differences are inherited/base-artifact changes and were excluded.
`Coverage.status` remains a modifier. No local Coverage-specific modifier flag changes were found. Inherited modifierExtension behavior is out of scope.

No material local summary flag changes were found for existing Coverage business elements. R6 new elements have their own summary flags but are covered by addition/representability findings or notable changes.
No local slicing changes were identified in the Coverage snapshot elements.
No fixed, pattern, or default value constraints were identified for local Coverage elements in either snapshot.

Serialization-breaking changes are concentrated in reported same-path type changes (`subscriberId`, `class.value`) and removed/split `payor`. No additional local serialization shape changes were found in the StructureDefinition comparison.
Major R6-only representability risks are reported. Full downgrade behavior would require an official ConceptMap and profile-specific extension policy.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Computable artifact status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The StructureDefinition identity and instance shape are unchanged by the metadata status value itself; it does not invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat this as a maturity/governance signal for R6 ballot review, not a data transform requirement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Coverage.identifier text no longer asserts uniqueness as strongly
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Cardinality and type remain `0..* Identifier`; no validation shape changes were found.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 definition/comment says the identifier is issued by the insurer and notes that not all insurers issue unique member IDs, so searches may return multiple responses. Systems relying on uniqueness should review matching/indexing assumptions.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Optional InsurancePlan reference added
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element is optional, so R4 instances can migrate to R6 without populating it.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 producers can now link a Coverage to an InsurancePlan directly; R4 downgrade requires an extension, a related resource convention, or loss of that link.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Coverage.period text recommends extensions for non-contiguous coverage periods
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element remains 0..1 Period with the same type and cardinality.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Applications needing multiple non-contiguous coverage periods should not expect native repeats in R6; the R6 text recommends extension use instead.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited changes in `language`, extension/modifierExtension rules, summary behavior, and base constraints were intentionally excluded from this Coverage report and should be assessed in the base artifact reports.
`Coverage.kind` is new, mandatory, and required-bound. Terminology review should confirm code meanings, expansion stability, and migration guidance for `insurance`, `self-pay`, and `other`.
A formal ConceptMap is needed for the payer split, `subscriberId` and `class.value` Identifier conversions, R6-only optional fields, and downgrade extension policy.
The StructureDefinition changes imply search/index changes, but SearchParameter compatibility is out of scope for this artifact report.
